extracted.intended_audience: journalists, corporate leaders, policymakers, and the general public interested in public-trust metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metrics for measuring and reporting public trust across institutions (government, business, media, NGOs) using the Edelman Trust Barometer methodology and audience segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Index
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Index is an average of a country’s trust in the institutions of government, business, media and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the headline metric for each country (example: Global 64). Presented alongside institution- and demographic-specific trust levels; can be trended year-to-year (country ranking, 2016-2018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust categories (TRUSTERS / NEUTRAL / DISTRUSTERS)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classifies countries or populations by their Trust Index score into three interpretive buckets for comparison and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional dimensions measured
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust is measured across the institutions of government, business, media and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports and analyses should present trust broken out by these institutions and discuss cross-institutional patterns (e.g., media becoming least-trusted institution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience segmentation: Informed Public
rubrics_metrics.description: All informed public respondents met the following criteria: aged 25-64, college-educated; household income in the top quartile for their age in their country; read or watch business/news media at least several times a week; follow public policy issues in the news at least several times a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting findings, distinguish the Informed Public from the mass population; comparisons between these segments are central to Trust Barometer analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience segmentation: Mass population
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass population respondents are aged 18+ and represent the portion of the population that do not meet the criteria for the Informed Public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this segment to report broader-population trust levels and contrast with the Informed Public to reveal differences in perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values basis / measurement reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Values based on percent trust; Values based on average percent trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether reported figures are raw percent-trust responses or averaged percent-trust indices; be consistent across charts and tables and annotate any year-over-year point changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media definition and component measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust Barometer respondents hold a broad definition of 'media' that can include platforms (social media, search engines) alongside journalism (publishers and news organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting media trust, break out components where possible (example percentages cited: social media 48% considered part of media; search engines 25%; journalism 89%). Note that overall trust in 'media' can decline even while trust in journalists rises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of misinformation and ability to identify credible news
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures include concern about fake news/false information (nearly seven in 10 respondents among the general population worry) and difficulty identifying whether a piece of news was produced by a respected media organization (59% say it is getting harder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these indicators to contextualize media-trust findings and to discuss the impact of misinformation on institutional credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility of sources and experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility measures for specific sources: journalists, CEOs, technical experts, financial industry analysts, successful entrepreneurs and 'a person like yourself' are tracked (examples: journalists rose 12 points; CEOs recorded a seven-percentage point gain; 'a person like yourself' dipped to an all-time low).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report source-specific credibility levels and changes over time to explain shifts in institutional trust; note thresholds mentioned (e.g., some experts now register credibility levels of 50% or higher).

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-level change and polarization indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: The Barometer flags polarization where country-level trust moves diverge — distinct splits between extreme trust gainers and losers (example: United States had a 37-point aggregate drop; China experienced a 27-point gain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight large aggregate changes and classify countries as gainers or losers; use these patterns to discuss global trends and national narratives.
